items.stem: At a high level, how does a diffusion model generate an image?

options.text: It starts from noise and iteratively denoises it toward an image matching the prompt
options.rationale: Correct: diffusion models learn to reverse a noising process, guided by the prompt.

options.text: It searches a database and returns the closest stored photo
options.rationale: It generates rather than retrieving existing images.

options.text: It renders a 3D model from CAD files
options.rationale: That is unrelated to diffusion image generation.

options.text: It copies pixels directly from the training set
options.rationale: It synthesises new images, not pixel copies.

items.explanation: Correct: diffusion models learn to reverse a noising process, guided by the prompt.

items.stem: Which TWO concerns should a team document before using generated images commercially? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Copyright and likeness rights of depicted content
options.rationale: Correct: generated content can raise copyright and likeness issues.
Correct: image models can reproduce harmful stereotypes.

options.text: The exact random seed is legally required on every asset
options.rationale: Seeds are a technical detail, not a legal requirement.

options.text: Images need no review if they look good
options.rationale: Appearance does not clear rights or bias concerns.

items.explanation: Correct: generated content can raise copyright and likeness issues.

items.stem: A designer wants to change only the background of an otherwise good image. Which technique fits best?

options.text: Inpainting the selected region while keeping the rest
options.rationale: Correct: inpainting edits a masked region and preserves the rest.

options.text: Regenerating the whole image from scratch
options.rationale: Full regeneration risks losing the good parts.
Quantisation is a compression step, not an editing tool.
Context window is irrelevant to image editing.

items.explanation: Correct: inpainting edits a masked region and preserves the rest.
